Chapter 15

Snapshots, and the promise they must not break

Making restart fast without letting the venue depend on a cache — and the fault-injection test that caught it depending on one.

By the end of this chapter

Build snapshots and recovery, and prove the snapshot is an optimisation rather than a source of truth.

Replaying a million commands on every restart would work and would take minutes. So the engine periodically writes a snapshot: the whole in-memory state, serialised, tagged with the sequence number it represents.

Recovery then becomes: load the newest snapshot, replay only the commands after it.

The promise

A snapshot is an optimisation and nothing more. The log remains sufficient on its own, and a corrupt or missing snapshot must cost replay *time* rather than *correctness*. The moment recovery genuinely needs a snapshot, the log has stopped being the system of record and the whole architecture has quietly become something else.

Fingerprinting the state

Rebuilding the book from a snapshot

Serialising the book as a nested structure of levels and queues would work and would be fragile — the invariants (sorted, total correct) would have to be preserved by the serialiser and trusted by the deserialiser.

Instead we serialise a flat list of orders and rebuild the book by resting each one in sequence order. The invariants are re-established by the same code that maintains them normally, so they cannot drift.

Bug found: a corrupt snapshot took the venue down

Every file in this project says the snapshot is an optimisation. A fault-injection test was written to prove it — write nonsense into engine_snapshot, then check recovery produces the same state as before.

The exception escaped recover and the engine would not start. The claim had been a claim; the property did not exist.

And one more test, so the others mean something

Vacuous tests are worse than no tests

A test that passes because the code path it exercises does not run is *actively harmful*: it is a green tick telling you something is proven when nothing is. Whenever a test asserts "X still works without Y", add a second test asserting Y exists.

Checkpoint

  • You can state what a snapshot is and what it is not
  • You can explain why the book is rebuilt by resting rather than deserialised directly
  • You can explain what a vacuous test is and how to guard against one
